summary: Calcipotriol (US generic name calcipotriene) is a synthetic vitamin D3 analogue applied topically for plaque psoriasis. It is rubbed gently into affected areas, typically once daily, and stopped once the psoriasis is controlled. Excessive application can be absorbed systemically and cause hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria, so weekly quantity, treated body surface area, and duration should be limited. It is available as a single agent and in fixed combination with the corticosteroid betamethasone dipropionate.
indications: Topical treatment of plaque psoriasis (as monotherapy or in fixed combination with betamethasone dipropionate, in patients 12 years and older)

dosage.t: Once daily for up to 4 weeks
dosage.n: Combination product: do not exceed 100 g per week; discontinue when control is achieved

dosage.t: Once daily for up to 4 weeks
dosage.n: Combination product: do not exceed 60 g per week
Treatment of more than 30% of body surface area is not recommended

admin: Rub an adequate layer into the affected area(s) gently and completely
Wash hands after application (unless the hands are being treated)
Discontinue therapy when psoriasis control is achieved

Not for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use
moa: Acts as a synthetic vitamin D3 analogue that binds the vitamin D receptor in keratinocytes, inhibiting their excessive proliferation and promoting normal differentiation; the precise mechanism in plaque psoriasis is not fully established.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to calcipotriol/calcipotriene or any component
relative: Extensive psoriasis or large treated body surface area
Application to face, groin, or axillae (combination product)
monitor: Serum and urinary calcium with extensive or prolonged use
Treated body surface area and weekly amount applied

preg: Limited human data are insufficient to evaluate drug-associated risk; oral calcipotriene in pregnant rats caused minor skeletal abnormalities (enlarged fontanelles, extra ribs). Use on the smallest area of skin for the shortest duration possible during pregnancy.
lact: No data on presence in human milk or effects on the breastfed infant; if used while breastfeeding, do not apply directly to the nipple or areola to avoid direct infant exposure.
renal: No specific topical dose adjustment, but systemic absorption with excessive use can disturb calcium homeostasis; monitor calcium with extensive or prolonged use.
hepatic: Calcipotriene undergoes rapid hepatic metabolism after systemic uptake; no specific topical dose adjustment is provided.

moderate: Other products containing calcipotriene or a corticosteroid - avoid concurrent use unless directed by a physician (combination product)
interactions.diagnostics: Excessive use can raise serum and urinary calcium; check calcium metabolism if hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria is suspected.

rare: Skin atrophy and HPA-axis suppression (with the corticosteroid combination)
Cataract or glaucoma (with the corticosteroid combination)
emergency: Symptomatic hypercalcemia (e.g., confusion, marked weakness, cardiac effects) from excessive systemic absorption

Wash your hands after applying (unless treating the hands)

Serum levels of parent drug generally below quantification; metabolite MC1080 detectable in some
Rapid hepatic metabolism after systemic uptake; not characterized topically

pearls: The US/FDA-approved generic name is calcipotriene; calcipotriol is the international (INN) name for the same molecule
Hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria can occur with excessive use - if they develop, stop treatment until calcium metabolism normalizes
Limit treatment to no more than 30% of body surface area and observe weekly dose caps
Often combined with betamethasone dipropionate for synergistic effect, but the combination adds corticosteroid risks (HPA suppression, skin atrophy)
Effects on calcium metabolism beyond 4 weeks of treatment have not been evaluated
missed: Apply the missed dose when remembered; if it is almost time for the next application, skip it and resume the once-daily schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topically applied product can be absorbed in amounts sufficient to produce systemic effects, chiefly hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria. Discontinue use, treat elevated calcium per standard measures, and monitor until calcium metabolism normalizes.
